items.proposed_content: Source-grounded: the zero count splits into a controlled average and an oscillatory part; unfolding removes changing density, after which GUE-type spacing evidence motivates a Hilbert–Pólya pair. Conceptual reading: a spectral model must explain residual statistics without defining its space from the zeros.

items.proposed_content: The natural spectral question is sharpened into an absorption model by three compatible constructions: first cohomology enters the function-field Lefschetz formula with a minus sign, exact-sequence additivity subtracts the cokernel zero spectrum from the regular representation, and semiclassical adelic periodization identifies the smooth zero count as a deficit of scaling states.

items.proposed_content: Moving from the weighted cokernel to an unweighted position-frequency cutoff changes the retained spectral information: the weighted model sees only critical-line zeros and truncates multiplicity according to delta, whereas the cutoff defect includes every zero with full multiplicity, representing off-line zeros by harmonic measure. Exact joint support in function fields is replaced at an Archimedean place by a thresholded prolate concentration space.

items.proposed_content: The zero spectrum arises from a linked Poisson-Mellin mechanism: compatible local homogeneous distributions form a restricted tensor product whose global normalization defect is the L-function; adelic Poisson summation gives the periodization map reciprocal rapid decay; Mellin orthogonality then becomes annihilation by the L-factor, forcing compactly supported dual cokernel distributions to be derivatives of point masses at its zeros, whose localized blocks assemble into the trace.

items.proposed_content: For positive-characteristic global fields, the proposed global cutoff trace asymptotic identifies a positive finite-cutoff defect with Weil's distribution, so the trace identity implies Weil positivity and RH; conversely, the zero-side cutoff calculation represents off-line zeros by nontrivial harmonic measures, while RH collapses them to point masses and recovers the trace identity.
